name: inprocess-obi-apb-rational-rate-timers-f1f4
description: One Ibex RVFI OBI CPU at its pinned 50 MHz declaration reaches two PULP APB3 timers declared at 30 MHz and 60 MHz in the same session. Neither pair has a whole half-period divider against 50 MHz (50:30 = 5:3, 50:60 = 5:6), so the entry places all three models on the exact common grid of lcm(50,30,60) = 300000000 Hz: one grid step is 1/(2 x 300000000) s, the reference CPU half period is 6 grid steps and one host tick advances 12 grid steps. The 30 MHz target is slower than the CPU (its half period is 10 grid steps, exactly 5/3 of a CPU half period) and the 60 MHz target is faster (5 grid steps, 5/6 of a CPU half period), so the faster model takes its own rising edges inside a single host tick: that is the sub-stepping. Each target's APB3 trace is sampled once per its own cycle and the per-case clockcase/summary state the measured rising-edge counts, so the 50:30 and 50:60 ratios are observations rather than assertions. No DMA and no IRQ behavior is declared, so F5/F6 are refused by name.
notes: The two target profiles are declared composition variants: same pinned PULP apb_timer RTL/source revision as configs/peripherals/pulp_timer, only the declared frequency_hz differs (30000000 and 60000000).  The pinned profile keeps its own 50000000 Hz declaration and is not edited; assume_single_clock is deliberately absent so the exact rational grid is the only admitted schedule.

The declared rates are 50000000, 30000000 and 60000000 Hz.  Their least common multiple is 300000000 Hz, so one grid step is 1/(2 x 300000000) s, the reference CPU half period is 300/50 = 6 grid steps, the 30 MHz target's is 300/30 = 10 and the 60 MHz target's is 300/60 = 5; one host tick advances 12 grid steps (exactly one CPU cycle).  The saved clock_plan.json states grid_lcm_hz, grid_steps_per_cpu_half, grid_steps_per_tick and each model's half period in grid steps and as an exact fraction of the CPU half period, so nothing is rounded.

The 60 MHz target is faster than the reference CPU (5 grid steps per half period against the CPU's 6), so its own rising edges fall inside a single host tick: five of its cycles per four CPU cycles, applied by the same phase schedule.  Its per-case rising-edge count is measured by the host and printed on the separate clockcase line and in the summary's clock_* fields; the case lines keep their historical bytes.
No behavior file and no DMA profile are declared: this scenario claims only F1-F4, and F5/F6 stay named refusals (unsupported-f5:target-irq-semantics:apb3:... and unsupported-f6:no-dma-model:APB3).

No record is routed to the 60 MHz target: this host reads a model's protocol outputs once per host tick, and that target's whole APB access window (psel/penable for two of its own cycles, plus a rsp_valid the bridge clears on its next edge) is 10 grid steps of the 12-step tick, so the window can fall between two samples.  A record routed to it is refused by name (unsupported-target-traffic:timer60:faster-than-reference-cpu:...) rather than run and timed out; see runs/p2-timing-20261103/refusals/faster-target-traffic.log.  The 30 MHz target is slower than the CPU and completes its real APB3 transfers in this same session.
